title: build: add -Dinstalled-exe-path for the Linux launcher files
body:
The Zig 0.17 port replaced the absolute path to the executable in the desktop file, D-Bus services and systemd user service with a bare  `ghostty`, since the install prefix is no longer known while the build  is configured. systemd resolves a bare ExecStart= name against a fixed search path rather than PATH: /usr/bin and /usr/local/bin on most systems, and only systemd's own directory on NixOS. So the service failed to start for any install outside those directories, including every Nix one.
    
-Dinstalled-exe-path gives the absolute path to write into those files. Without it they still name the executable alone, which is right for packages installing to /usr. The Nix package passes its output path, and the Flatpak manifests pass /app/bin/ghostty, which is what they produced before the port.

Fixes #14805

AI disclosure: Claude Code was used in the preparation of this PR.

files.patch:
@@ -123,6 +123,14 @@ relevant to package maintainers:
   version, glibc, etc. Run `zig targets` to a get a full list of available
   targets.
 
+- `-Dinstalled-exe-path=$prefix/bin/ghostty`: The absolute path the
+  `ghostty` executable will be installed at, written into the desktop file,
+  D-Bus service and systemd user service on Linux. The build can't work this
+  out from `--prefix` itself. Without it, those files name the executable
+  alone (`ghostty`), and systemd only looks for that in standard directories
+  such as `/usr/bin` and `/usr/local/bin`. Set it for any other prefix, and
+  leave `DESTDIR` out of it.
+

@@ -12,6 +12,7 @@
   pkg-config,
   zig_0_17,
   pandoc,
+  systemd,
   revision ? "dirty",
   optimize ? "debug",
   enableX11 ? true,
@@ -92,6 +93,7 @@ in
       "-Dcpu=baseline"
       "-Doptimize=${optimize}"
       "-Dstrip=${lib.boolToString strip}"
+      "-Dinstalled-exe-path=${placeholder "out"}/bin/ghostty"
     ];
 
     outputs = [
@@ -129,6 +131,47 @@ in
       echo "gst_all_1.gst-plugins-good" >> "$out/nix-support/propagated-user-env-packages"
     '';
 
+    # The systemd, D-Bus and desktop files launch Ghostty by the path given
+    # in -Dinstalled-exe-path. systemd only searches its own directory for a
+    # bare name on NixOS, so check that every one of them names an
+    # executable that exists.
+    doInstallCheck = stdenv.hostPlatform.isLinux;
+
+    nativeInstallCheckInputs = [systemd];
+
+    installCheckPhase = ''
+      runHook preInstallCheck
+
+      # The verifier starts a user manager, which needs somewhere to keep
+      # its runtime state; the sandbox gives it no /run. dbus.socket and
+      # graphical-session.target aren't in the sandbox either, so only the
+      # unit itself is checked, including its ExecStart.
+      export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$TMPDIR/run" HOME="$TMPDIR/home"
+      mkdir -p -m 0700 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR" "$HOME"
+      for unit in "$out"/share/systemd/user/*.service; do
+        # Its messages are colored and end in a carriage return, which
+        # `nix build -L` shows as a blank line, so strip both.
+        status=0
+        output=$(SYSTEMD_COLORS=0 systemd-analyze --user verify --man=no --recursive-errors=no "$unit" 2>&1) || status=$?
+        [[ -z "$output" ]] || echo "''${output//$'\r'/}" >&2
+        if ((status != 0)); then
+          exit "$status"
+        fi
+      done
+
+      for file in "$out"/share/dbus-1/services/*.service "$out"/share/applications/com.mitchellh.ghostty*.desktop; do
+        while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
+          exe=''${value%% *}
+          if [[ "$exe" != /* || ! -x "$exe" ]]; then
+            echo "$file: $key does not name an executable: $exe" >&2
+            exit 1
+          fi
+        done < <(grep -E '^(TryExec|Exec)=' "$file")
+      done
+
+      runHook postInstallCheck
+    '';
+
     meta = {
       homepage = "https://ghostty.org";
       license = lib.licenses.mit;

@@ -40,6 +40,11 @@ exe_entrypoint: ExeEntrypoint = .ghostty,
 version: std.SemanticVersion = .{ .major = 0, .minor = 0, .patch = 0 },
 lib_version: std.SemanticVersion = .{ .major = 0, .minor = 0, .patch = 0 },
 
+/// The absolute path the Ghostty executable is installed at, for the Linux
+/// desktop, D-Bus and systemd files that launch it. Null means they name
+/// the executable alone.
+installed_exe_path: ?[]const u8 = null,
+
 /// Binary properties
 pie: bool = false,
 strip: bool = false,
@@ -352,6 +357,27 @@ pub fn init(b: *std.Build, appVersion: []const u8, libVersion: []const u8) !Conf
     else
         try std.SemanticVersion.parse(libVersion);
 
+    // The install prefix is only known once the build runs, too late to
+    // write it into the files that launch Ghostty, so a build installing
+    // anywhere systemd doesn't search has to say where the executable goes.
+    config.installed_exe_path = b.option(
+        []const u8,
+        "installed-exe-path",
+        "Absolute path the ghostty executable will be installed at, written " ++
+            "into the Linux desktop, D-Bus and systemd files. If not specified, " ++
+            "they name the executable alone, which systemd only finds in " ++
+            "/usr/bin or /usr/local/bin.",
+    );
+    if (config.installed_exe_path) |exe_path| {
+        if (!std.fs.path.isAbsolute(exe_path)) {
+            std.log.err(
+                "-Dinstalled-exe-path must be an absolute path, got '{s}'",
+                .{exe_path},
+            );
+            return error.InvalidInstalledExePath;
+        }
+    }
+
     //---------------------------------------------------------------
     // Binary Properties
